  • Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

  • AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

  • Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

  • Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.

What we offer

  • Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

  • Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

  • Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

  • Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

  • Annual company offsite: Each year, we bring the entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia and Italy.

  • Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

This role is remote and can be executed globally. If you prefer, you can work from our offices in Bangalore, Dublin, London, New York, San Francisco, Tokyo, and Warsaw.

About ElevenLabs

ElevenLabs is a research and product company defining the frontier of Audio AI. Millions of individuals use ElevenLabs to read articles, voice over their videos, and reclaim voices lost from disability. And the leading developers and enterprises use ElevenLabs to create AI agents for support, sales, and education.

ElevenLabs is only 2 years old and scaling rapidly. We are just getting started. If you want to work hard and have an incredible impact, we would love to hear from you.

This role goes beyond producing individual assets. You’ll develop strong visual concepts, translate them into flexible design systems and toolkits, and ensure they work consistently across formats and teams. You’ll join the Brand Design team and collaborate closely with Marketing, Product Design, Video, Events, and other teams across the company.

You will work closely with Nev Flynn and Marina Kondratenko from the Design Team, as well as members of the Growth Team and Operations Teams to support asset creation.

  • Develop visual concepts and creative directions for product launches, campaigns, events, and other high-visibility projects.

  • Evolve ElevenLabs’ visual identity and translate it into scalable design systems, toolkits, and guidelines.

  • A keen eye for detail and a passion for creating polished, high-quality work.

jobs.title: Senior Product Designer
jobs.description_html:
About the role

You'll own the end-to-end design of features that millions of people use to create, teach, and persuade. From early 0-to-1 explorations to polished refinements at scale, you'll collaborate daily with PMs, engineers, and designers to scope, prototype, test, and ship across Gamma's core product surfaces.

This role demands someone who can move fast and light: creating quick prototypes, running lean experiments, and iterating based on data to hit measurable outcomes. You'll balance speed with craft, knowing when to polish pixels and when to ship and learn. If you've designed for modern productivity tools and understand how people actually work, you'll thrive here.

Our team has a strong in-office culture and works in person 4–5 days per week in San Francisco. We love working together to stay creative and connected, with flexibility to work from home when focus matters most.

What you'll do

  • Own problem areas from concept to launch, producing flows, wireframes, and high-fidelity specs with an eye for usability and craft

  • Collaborate with PMs, engineers, and designers to scope, design, prototype, test, and ship features across core product surfaces

  • Define success criteria and ship features that move activation, retention, or conversion

  • Create quick prototypes and run lean experiments, iterating based on data to drive measurable outcomes

  • Partner tightly with engineering to ensure designs are feasible, performant, and maintainable

  • Conduct user research, usability testing, and design critiques to validate and refine solutions

What you'll bring

  • 5+ years of end-to-end product design experience with a strong portfolio showing shipped work, ideally on productivity or workflow tools

  • Proficiency in Figma and modern prototyping tools with the ability to produce clear specs and collaborate closely with engineering

  • Metrics-minded approach with experience setting success criteria and shipping features that moved key product metrics

  • Strong visual design skills with attention to detail, an understanding of design systems, and the judgment to balance craft with velocity

  • Experience working in small, fast-paced teams where you owned projects from research through shipped UI

  • Familiarity with modern productivity tools or ecosystems like Notion, Craft, or similar, with an understanding of how users actually work in these products

  • Fluency with AI-powered design tools and workflows — actively keeping up with the evolving landscape (e.g., AI prototyping, generative design, etc.) and folding the best of it into your process

Compensation range:

The base salary for this full-time position, which spans multiple internal levels depending on qualifications, ranges between $180K - $260K plus benefits & equity.

Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors, including but not limited to experience and expertise in the requirements listed above.

If you're interested in this role but you don't meet every requirement, we encourage you to apply anyway! We're always excited about meeting great people.

  • Partner with the Senior Design Systems Designer to scale Harvey's visual language and support the rollout of new system foundations across the product.

  • Collaborate with product designers and frontend engineers to ensure system components are intuitive to use, accurately implemented, and consistently adopted.

  • Own and create polished production assets, libraries, prototypes, and documentation that enable teams to build quickly and with confidence.

  • Support AI-assisted design workflows by preparing components, documentation, and system assets that are optimized for both designers and AI tools.

  • Maintain the quality and health of the design system through QA, organization, continuous refinement, and operational improvements.

  • Advocate for exceptional craftsmanship, consistency, and usability across every product surface.

What You Have

  • 3–5 years of experience as a Product Designer, Production Designer, UI Designer, or Design Systems Designer working on digital products.

  • Exceptional visual craft with a meticulous eye for detail, layout, spacing, consistency, and production quality.

  • Exceptional organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple workstreams while maintaining a high quality bar.

  • Experience building and maintaining component libraries and design systems in Figma, including auto layout, variables, components, and variants.

  • Curiosity and experience in AI-assisted design tools and evolving implementation workflows, you don't need to be an engineer, but you're excited about where the discipline is heading.

  • Excellent collaboration and communication skills, with a desire to learn through close partnership with design and engineering.

  • Comfort working in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment and enthusiasm for helping shape an evolving Design Systems practice.

We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

Harvey designs and builds for a legal industry being reshaped by AI, moving with the urgency and ambition the moment demands, not just adapting to change but architecting it. As a Design Systems Designer at Harvey, you will define the foundations that make our product coherent, scalable, and trustworthy as it grows in complexity. The design system is not just a library of components. It is the shared language between design, engineering, and AI that ensures consistency, quality, and confidence across every interaction.

This is a design role with unusual technical depth. You lead with design: craft, systems thinking, and a strong point of view on product experience. But you're equally at home in architecture and implementation. You understand how tokens are structured, how components are composed, and how systems are built to scale, and you use that fluency to push the system forward rather than hand decisions over the wall.

We're looking for someone who has lived through the evolution of the discipline, someone who understands not just how modern design systems work, but why they're built the way they are, and where the field is heading, especially as AI-native products reshape what a design system needs to be.

This role will report to the Design org, and will be based in SF, NYC, or Toronto.


What you’ll do

  1. Build an AI-native design system that sets the bar for design quality for Design, Engineering, and Product through technical direction and collaboration

    • Design, prototype, and ship production-ready system components in tight collaboration with frontend and platform engineering, with shared ownership of quality, performance, and maintainability

    • Define and evolve the core design system foundations (components, patterns, and tokens) that scale across complex, AI-powered experiences

    • Push both the architecture and the implementation of the system: shape component APIs, token structure, theming, and composition patterns alongside engineering, not downstream of it

    • Advocate for technical approaches with confidence, especially in new or ambiguous territory where established patterns don't yet exist

    • Embed accessibility, responsiveness, and performance into the system by default

    • Establish clear contribution, governance, and deprecation models that balance velocity with system integrity

    • Raise the bar for system quality across the product through design reviews, critique, and hands-on work

    • Build alignment across Design, Engineering, and Product through technical direction and collaboration

    • Anticipate future product and platform needs, evolving the system proactively as Harvey scales

  2. Own AI design and implementation workflows for the design team, establishing best practices for prototyping and shipping with AI

    • Establish in-code prototyping patterns that make it easier to be innovative and consistent as designers increasingly leverage IDEs to experiment and ship.

    • Define AI-assisted design and implementation workflows, establishing best practices for prototyping and shipping with AI

    • Document system usage and best practices in a way that is clear, practical, and trusted by product teams

What you have

  • 5+ years (Senior) / 8+ years (Staff) of product design experience, with significant ownership of design systems in complex product environments

  • A design portfolio that demonstrates high design craft in system-level thinking, but a strong point of view on quality, and visual cohesion

  • Deep design systems expertise, including an understanding of the history and evolution of the discipline. You know why the field moved from style guides to tokens to composable architectures, and you have a point of view on what comes next

  • Excellent design engineering communication: you articulate system decisions and tradeoffs fluently to designers, engineers, and cross-functional partners

  • Ability to clearly articulate system decisions and tradeoffs to designers, engineers, and cross-functional partners

  • Strong knowledge of scalable system architecture and component implementation: component API design, design tokens, theming strategies, and how systems hold up across teams and codebases

  • Design Engineer experience preferred, but not required in an AI-first world where the boundary between design and engineering is shifting

  • High ownership: you treat the system as a product, not a ticket queue

  • Strong opinions, loosely held, being comfortable challenging conventions and evolving best practices as the discipline changes

  • Comfort operating in ambiguous problem spaces and bringing structure where it doesn't yet exist

Why design systems matter at Harvey

Harvey is an AI-native product. As the system reasons, responds, and adapts in real time, the interface must remain consistent and legible. A strong design system ensures that complexity does not leak into the experience. It enables teams to move faster, reduces cognitive load for users, and builds trust in moments where clarity matters most.

Compensation

$205,760 - $315,000 USD

jobs.description_html:
Why Harvey

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

We're looking for a Senior Manager, Product Design to lead two parts of Harvey: our Admin experience and our Platform design system team.

Admin is how firm leaders and innovation teams configure, govern, and scale Harvey inside their organizations, from workflow configuration to usage visibility. These champions are the main decision makers in whether Harvey succeeds at an account, and Admin is where they turn their investment into measurable return. The team also owns our knowledge platform and how legal connectors get integrated into Harvey. A general model can reason about law. But it can't reach a firm's precedent, its matter files, or the systems its lawyers work in every day. Making that context usable is the moat in legal AI, and design decides how much of it a lawyer can actually get to.

Platform is the spine of the design team. It defines how we work in an AI-native way and sets the standard every product team builds on. Most design systems are run as a service: product teams decide what to build, the system team supplies the parts. On an AI-native team, the system sets the craft bar instead of serving it, and its users aren't only designers. When anyone in EPD can generate an interface, the system is what keeps quality consistent and gets teams to a shipped implementation faster. Building that is one of the highest-leverage jobs at Harvey, and you'll shape the team around it. You'll own the system every team builds from and the AI tooling that changes what a designer can produce.

You'll report to the VP Design as a foundational member of the Design leadership team, with portfolio-wide impact on how our product, team, and culture scale. You'll set the operating bar for how we work, and lay foundations for the product that hold for years.

What You'll Do

Own Admin as a product

  • Drive strategy and execution for the Admin platform in close partnership with Product and Engineering, rooted in how champions actually run Harvey inside their firms.

  • Work directly with customers, research, and usage data to find where champions lose time or lose confidence, and design the workflow configuration, knowledge management, and visibility experiences that fix it.

  • Tie your roadmap to customer outcomes: faster rollout, wider adoption, and evidence of ROI our champions can take to their own leadership.

Own the system, not the service

  • Define Harvey's design system as a set of product decisions: what good looks like for AI-powered legal work, encoded as patterns product teams inherit rather than requests they submit.

  • Set the craft bar across interaction, systems thinking, content design, and visual execution, and hold it as our surface area grows.

  • Build the governance model that lets the system move fast without fragmenting: contribution paths, adoption expectations, and clear calls on when a team may deviate.

Own AI tooling for the design org

  • Decide how Harvey's designers use AI: what tools we adopt, what we build ourselves, and what the new default workflow looks like from problem to prototype.

  • Raise the floor and the ceiling. Make the whole team faster, and make it possible for a single designer to ship things that used to take a pod.

  • Treat this as a live experiment with real rigor. Try things, measure them, kill what doesn't work, and share what does across EPD.

Build and lead the team

  • Build, grow, and develop a team of high-craft ICs across systems, product, and prototyping from a small starting footprint.

  • Own org design, resourcing, and prioritization across four surfaces with very different rhythms, including the conference deadlines that don't move.

  • Give strategic, systems-level feedback on end-to-end flows, not just screens.

Lead across the org

  • Partner with design, product, and engineering leaders to evolve how Harvey builds, and represent Platform in high-stakes conversations with executives and customers.

  • Establish how we make design decisions in high-trust, high-stakes environments where clarity and accuracy are non-negotiable.

  • Be a foundational member of the Design leadership team and help set the operating model the rest of the org runs on.

What You Have

  • 8-10+ years in Product Design, with 5+ years directly managing product designers.

  • Experience owning a design system at real scale, including the political work of getting it adopted.

  • Experience designing and shipping AI-powered or highly technical products.

  • A strong portfolio showing leadership of complex products from concept through launch, with clear impact on users and the business.

  • Fluency with AI tooling in your own practice, and a real opinion about how it changes design work.

  • Proven experience leading design strategy and execution alongside Product and Engineering.

  • Demonstrated ability to define and ship high-quality experiences in complex, ambiguous problem spaces.

  • Excellent judgment about when to go deep, when to delegate, and when to push.

  • Exceptional communication skills and the ability to influence senior stakeholders, internally and in front of customers.

  • Deep commitment to growing people and raising the craft bar across a team.

  • Comfort operating in fast-moving environments with evolving priorities.

  • Empathy for users, teammates, and the realities of high-stakes professional work.

  • A growth mindset, resilience, and a bias toward learning through doing.

  • Strong people leadership instincts with a bias toward clarity, empathy, and accountability.

Compensation

$235,500 - $325,000 USD

Founded in 2019, Linear has become the platform of choice for more than 40,000 companies (including OpenAI, Coinbase, and Ramp) to plan, build, and ship their products. Today, our team is distributed across North America, Europe, and Australia, and we’re continuing to grow internationally. What unites us is relentless focus, fast execution, and a deep care for software craftsmanship.

Quality is our competitive advantage. Every member of our fully remote team is a maker at heart, caring deeply about the quality and feel of our work. While the industry optimizes for speed and metrics alone, we believe that craft and quality have lasting value. Quality creates gravity — it pulls people toward our team and product rather than requiring us to push. This philosophy drives everything we do, from product decisions to hiring choices.

For this role, we expect robust design skills, sharp product thinking, and the ability to engage in technical discussions. We work in small, autonomous project teams, where engineers are paired tightly with designers to explore ideas, build prototypes, deploy internal builds, and ultimately ship to customers. You will be a key element of projects from beginning to end.

Location & work mode

Linear is a remote-first company, with optional co-working offices in San Francisco, New York, and London. This role is open to candidates based in North America. You can work from anywhere within this region. We value deep focus and async collaboration, with intentional moments to connect in person through team off-sites, optional co-working, and occasional travel.

What you'll do

  • Pair closely with engineering and product to initiate and complete roadmap projects, no hand-offs

  • Spot opportunities to redesign or refine key screens and flows, as well as smaller quality issues and “paper cuts” as you use Linear

  • Create mockups, prototypes, and high-fidelity visuals to communicate ideas and describe their execution

  • Guide and inspire fellow designers through collaborative critique of work-in-progress

  • Use and improve our lightweight design system components

  • Help with hiring new teammates that can elevate our team and product

What we’re looking for

  • 7+ years experience designing software

  • Courage to ask questions, experiment, and advocate for what you feel is right

  • Humility to accept feedback, adapt your thinking, and iterate toward the best solution

  • Experience with prototyping in Figma (and beyond with tools like AI, HTML/CSS, Origami)

  • Ability to distill problems and feedback, then design clear, focused solutions

  • Effective written and verbal communication skills — much of our work is async

What we offer

We're a small, focused team that cares deeply about the quality of our work and the people we do it with. Here's what you can expect:

  • Competitive salary and equity

  • Employee-friendly equity terms including early exercise in the US and extended exercise windows

  • Daily meal and coffee stipend on every workday

  • Paid co-working space or desk

  • Health coverage (based on country requirements)

  • 5 weeks paid vacation, plus local statutory holidays

  • 4 months paid parental leave

  • Paid month off after 4 years & every 2 years thereafter

  • Regular team events and off-sites

  • Remote-first with no required commute

jobs.title: Brand Designer, Creative Studio
jobs.description_html:
Who We Are

Notion is the collaborative AI workspace where teams and agents think together. We're building one place where your knowledge, projects, meetings, and AI tools live side by side, so work is faster, clearer, and less fragmented. Millions of individuals, small teams, and large companies run their work on Notion.

Notinos (our employees) are customer zero in bringing this future of work to life. We care about craft, building things that last, and the belief that great work is still fundamentally human. Our goal isn’t to ship the next feature. Each and every team of Notinos is working to set the standard for how humans work together in the AI era. From building a business’s system of record to making and managing AI agents to automating away the busy work, we care deeply about giving our customers more time for their life’s work.

About the Role

This role is based in New York City. We work from our offices on Mondays, Tuesdays and Thursdays (our Anchor Days) because we do our best thinking and building together in person. We’re looking for someone who’s excited to work alongside the team during those days.

This role sits on Notion’s Creative Studio, a small team of designers, illustrators, and filmmakers. Our work tells the story of our offering in a way that reflects the products themselves: smart, refined, and with a dash of wit on the side.

As a Brand Designer, you’ll work on high-impact brand initiatives and campaigns: setting direction from early strategy through final execution, partnering closely with stakeholders and executives, and raising the bar for craft and systems. You’ll be asked to define approaches, resolve ambiguity, and influence both project outcomes and how the team works.

What You'll Achieve

  • Concept, art direct and design high-visibility moments from brand campaigns, product launches, and events, developing approaches that can scale across a broad range of surfaces, moments, and channels.

  • Contribute to our brand systems and develop standards and tooling that improve velocity and consistency for teammates near and far.

  • Mentor and raise the bar for other designers and creative partners through feedback, critique, and patterns that make great work repeatable.

Skills You'll Need to Bring

  • 10+ years in an agency or in-house environment, with demonstrated leadership on ambiguous, complex, high-impact work.

  • A strong portfolio of work that’s culturally resonant and visually diverse, and that showcases your ability to tell stories across many channels.

  • A deep commitment to systems thinking, typographic excellence, and sensitivity to small details.

  • Experience working with a broad range of makers. You’ve teamed up with illustrators, animators, copywriters, filmmakers, photographers, and beyond to bring your ideas to life.

  • Excellent partnership skills. You can work hand-in-hand with cross-functional stakeholders, drive alignment, and make pragmatic tradeoffs.

  • A tinkerer’s mindset. You're curious about how your tools are evolving and have a strong perspective on how AI can expand creative expression and drive production. You’ll actively experiment with new AI workflows to concept, prototype, and push our design systems further.

Notion is committed to providing highly competitive cash compensation, equity, and benefits. The compensation offered for this role will be based on multiple factors such as location, the role’s scope and complexity, and the candidate’s experience and expertise, and may vary from the range provided below. For roles based in New York City, the estimated base salary range for this role is $200,000 - $250,000 per year.

By clicking “Submit Application”, I understand and agree that Notion and its affiliates and subsidiaries will collect and process my information in accordance with Notion’s Global Recruiting Privacy Policy and NYLL 144.

#LI-Onsite

A Note on AI

You don’t need deep AI expertise for every role, but we do expect every Notino to be intellectually curious, drawn to tinkering and discovery, and excited to use AI as a real collaborator in their work. For some roles, AI fluency is a core requirement — when that’s the case, we'll say so explicitly in the qualifications. People who thrive here don’t treat AI as a novelty. They use it to think better, and make their work easier for others to build on.

Equal Opportunity & Accommodations

We hire talented people from a wide range of backgrounds. If you’re excited about this role but don’t meet every bullet, we still encourage you to apply. Notion is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of any legally protected characteristic. Consistent with applicable law, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records. Notion provides reasonable accommodations during the application process; if you need one, please let your recruiter know.

Notion is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate in hiring or any employment decision based on race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), marital status, ancestry, physical or mental disability, genetic information, veteran status, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. About The Role

Imagine yourself in the 1970s or 80s thinking through how computing should look and feel for people who had never seen one before. That's what we're trying to do at Notion — make software that feels timeless, with the craftsmanship of German cameras, playfulness of Japanese toys, and mass appeal of Coca-Cola. We have no end of fascinating challenges that can only be solved by someone with innate product & UX sense, technical aptitude, great taste, and impeccable craft.

 

This role can be based in either San Francisco or New York City. We work from our offices on Mondays, Tuesdays and Thursdays (our Anchor Days) because we do our best thinking and building together in person. We’re looking for someone who’s excited to work alongside the team during those days.

What You'll Achieve:

  • Design product concepts that balance vision, craft, speed, and business potential.

  • Craft every detail of new product features, from idea to UX to pixel-perfect execution.

  • Run projects end to end with engineers to drive your vision to the ship line.

  • Partner closely with our Customer Experience, Sales, and Customer Success teams to understand what each of our diverse user segments need, want, and love about Notion. Use this data and acquired intuition to prioritize, plan, and scope our product roadmap.

  • Work with Marketing to devise new ways to tell great stories throughout the user lifecycle, and across our site, product, help guides and other channels.

  • Create new patterns that are intuitive, practical, and convergent. Evolve our design system intentionally as we scale.

Skills You'll Need to Bring:

  • You have well-rounded skills and experience to run projects independently end to end. 5+ years of working experience.

  • You seek to understand the needs of customers then explore and advocate for the strongest user experiences to solve their problems

  • You enjoy untangling vague conceptual problems and have a sharp intuition for the most accessible mental models and flows, so users can immediately start gaining value out of the product.

  • You create clear, intuitive, and visually appealing human interfaces.

  • You care about business needs, implications, and practicality of your designs. You don't get stuck on pretty UI or deep abstractions and can balance between craft, speed, and the bottom line.

  • You have strong beliefs, loosely held. You're a good listener who collaborates well with different stakeholders. You observe and internalize all inputs and feedback to help you reach an optimal decision.

  • You understand how to tell stories using both words and visuals, and strategize the best ways to drive alignment.

  • You value working cross-functionally with project management, engineering, research and data — as well as design peers.

Nice to Haves:

  • You've designed and built great tools with small teams in the past.

  • You bring unique strengths and perspectives to the team. We're looking to build a diverse team where our skills and experience can complement each other.

  • You've experienced the pain of fragmented tools and information silos created by them, and have a strong urge to fix it.

  • You're familiar with the work of computing heroes like Douglas Engelbart, Alan Kay, Bret Victor, etc. — and understand why we're big fans.

  • You are a designer who can code!

jobs.title: Physical Design Engineer, Forward Deployed Engineering
jobs.description_html:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Forward Deployed Engineering team partners with leading semiconductor companies to deploy production-grade AI systems across the entire chip design lifecycle: design, verification, and physical design. We operate at the intersection of customer delivery and core platform development, embedding deeply with customers to translate frontier model capabilities into systems that materially improve engineering workflows and accelerate innovation.

Our work turns early, high-touch deployments into repeatable solution patterns, reference architectures, and evaluation practices that scale across the semiconductor ecosystem.

About the Role

We are seeking a highly skilled Physical Design Engineer to join our semiconductor-focused Forward Deployed Engineering team. This is a senior IC role that will begin with a strong emphasis on physical design expertise, technical judgment, advisory leverage, and customer credibility, with the expectation that the person will grow into a broader Forward Deployed Engineering role over time.

In the near term, you will serve as the team’s physical design SME across semiconductor deployments: helping FDEs, Product, and Research understand backend implementation workflows, pressure-test AI-assisted solution ideas against real physical design constraints, and raise the quality of our customer-facing technical work. You will help the broader team build fluency in implementation flows, EDA tooling, signoff methodology, and the trade-offs that shape physical design decisions in practice.

Over time, we expect this role to expand beyond SME support into broader FDE ownership: partnering directly with customers, shaping deployment strategy, building and iterating production-grade AI systems, driving technical workstreams, and helping turn high-touch semiconductor deployments into repeatable solutions.

This is a strong fit for someone who brings deep physical design expertise today and is excited to grow into a customer-facing, systems-building, delivery-oriented FDE role.

In this role, you will:

  • Serve as the physical design SME for semiconductor customer engagements, helping FDE teams understand backend implementation workflows, constraints, and opportunities

  • Partner with FDEs during customer discovery and scoping to translate ambiguous pain points into clear solution hypotheses, success criteria, and technical plans

  • Support customer-facing technical conversations as a trusted advisor, engaging credibly with technical leaders

  • Help shape AI-assisted solutions across physical design workflows, including floorplanning, place and route, clocking, timing closure, congestion, power, physical verification, and signoff

  • Guide feasibility and integration decisions across the entire chip design lifecycle: design, verification, and physical design

  • Partner with FDEs and customer SMEs to curate evaluation datasets, golden tasks, rubrics, and acceptance criteria for physical design use cases, ensuring evals reflect real workflows and meaningful success metrics

  • Build or guide lightweight prototypes, benchmarks, methodology experiments, and internal tools that validate opportunities and accelerate solution development

  • Educate and mentor the broader FDE team on physical design concepts, implementation flows, EDA tooling, and key trade-offs so the org can engage customers with greater depth and confidence

  • Surface repeated customer signal to Product and Research to help shape roadmap, model behavior, and platform capabilities for semiconductor use cases

  • Progressively take on broader FDE responsibilities, including customer discovery, solution architecture, prototype development, production deployment, and ownership of technical workstreams

Minimum Qualifications

  • BS with 7+ years, MS with 5+ years, or equivalent industry experience in physical design, physical implementation, or backend signoff for complex ASIC or SoC programs

  • Demonstrated success bringing complex designs through tapeout, with hands-on experience in floorplanning, place and route, CTS, timing closure, power analysis, physical verification, and signoff

  • Deep familiarity with industry-standard EDA tools and flows for synthesis, PNR, STA, physical verification, equivalence checking, and power analysis

  • Strong understanding of how physical design intersects with microarchitecture, RTL, verification, design methodology, libraries/PDKs, and system-level PPA trade-offs

  • Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to translate deep technical trade-offs clearly in customer-facing and cross-functional settings

  • Comfortable operating as a consultative expert and advisor — unblocking teams, shaping decisions, and raising technical quality without necessarily being the direct implementation owner

  • Strong scripting and automation skills in Python, Tcl, or similar

  • Excited to grow beyond domain SME responsibilities into a broader Forward Deployed Engineering role, including hands-on solution building, customer-facing delivery, and ownership of deployment outcomes

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience working across multiple semiconductor companies, design environments, or tool stacks, with a point of view shaped by different engineering cultures and methodologies

  • Experience partnering with external customers, strategic accounts, or design partners in a technical advisory capacity

  • Experience defining or scaling evaluation workflows, benchmarks, or acceptance criteria

  • Exposure to adjacent workflows such as design and/or verification

  • Experience applying AI/LLM systems to semiconductor workflows

  • Prior experience in solutions engineering, field engineering, customer-facing technical delivery, or consultative technical roles

About OpenAI

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity.

jobs.title: Product Designer, Accessibility
jobs.description_html:
About the Team

OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. The Design Systems team creates the foundations that help teams across OpenAI build coherent, high-quality experiences at scale.

Accessibility is fundamental to that work. We’re building the shared standards, components, tools, and practices that make inclusive experiences the default across OpenAI’s products and platforms.

About the Role

In this role, you’ll lead OpenAI’s company-wide accessibility program from within Design Foundations. You’ll pair strategy and organizational influence with hands-on product design—advocating for disabled people, removing barriers across complete customer journeys, and establishing durable ownership throughout the company.

This is an opportunity to define accessibility for a new generation of products spanning web, mobile, desktop, voice, AI, and hardware. You’ll help teams consider the many ways people perceive, understand, navigate, and interact with technology, going beyond minimum compliance to create experiences that are genuinely useful and inclusive.

Working across design, engineering, research, product, go-to-market, and legal, you’ll make accessibility an expected part of product quality—not a final review or the responsibility of a single expert.

This role is based in our San Francisco HQ. We offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role you will:

  • Define OpenAI’s accessibility strategy, roadmap, governance, priorities, and measures of progress.

  • Design and ship accessible experiences while identifying systemic barriers across complete customer journeys.

  • Build accessibility into our design system through inclusive components, tokens, interaction patterns, Figma libraries, documentation, and engineering guardrails.

  • Center disabled people through participatory research, usability studies, and assistive-technology testing rather than relying solely on assumptions, simulations, or automated tools.

  • Design for permanent, temporary, and situational disabilities, including multiple ways to perceive information, navigate interfaces, understand content, and complete important tasks.

  • Establish practical standards for screen readers, keyboard navigation, focus, reading order, contrast, typography, motion, captions, forms, errors, and multimodal interactions.

  • Lead accessibility audits, remediation priorities, launch readiness, and continuous validation across platforms.

  • Partner with go-to-market, legal, compliance, and product teams on enterprise readiness, accessibility documentation, procurement needs, and customer commitments.

  • Grow company-wide capability through training, critiques, engineering partnerships, and a network of accessibility champions.

jobs.description_html:
About the Team

Our Robotics team is focused on unlocking general-purpose robotics and pushing towards AGI-level intelligence in dynamic, real-world settings. We are seeking an Actuator Gear Design Engineer to lead the development of custom gears and gear stages for advanced robotic systems. You will own actuator development from early architecture and concept generation through prototype validation and system integration, partnering closely with mechanical, electrical, controls, firmware, and reliability teams. You will partner with external suppliers and internal manufacturing to create full gearbox assemblies.

This role focuses on the design, integration, and validation of precision gearing, including broader knowledge around motor electromagnetics, transmission types, sensing, structural components, and thermal architectures. You will help drive actuator development across the full engineering lifecycle while establishing scalable design, test, and integration practices for future robotic platforms.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA, and requires in-person presence 4 days a week.

In this role, you will:

  • Lead the architecture, design, and integration of custom robotic actuator gearing.

  • Define actuator requirements and system-level trade studies around torque density, bandwidth, efficiency, thermal performance, back drivability, inertia, reliability, manufacturability, and cost.

  • Design precision electromechanical assemblies with strong attention to tolerances, alignment, load paths, thermal expansion, sealing, wear, and serviceability.

  • Drive actuator integration into robotic systems, partnering closely with controls, firmware, electrical, and robotics software teams to optimize closed-loop performance.

  • Develop and evaluate architectures with integrated sensing and encoder strategies.

  • Build and validate prototypes through hands-on bring-up, debugging, characterization, and iterative refinement.

  • Develop test methodologies and characterization infrastructure for actuator performance, reliability, durability, and failure analysis.

  • Analyze test data to identify limitations, failure modes, and opportunities for design improvement.

  • Collaborate with manufacturing and supplier partners to transition designs from prototype to scalable production-ready assemblies.

  • Support DFM, DFA, DFT, calibration, and assembly strategies for electromechanical subsystems.

  • Contribute to actuator sourcing strategy, vendor qualification, prototype builds, and supply-chain development.

  • Document designs, interfaces, validation results, and engineering decisions to support long-term maintainability and production readiness.

  • Help establish engineering standards, integration practices, and development workflows for future robotic platforms.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have strong intuition for designing high-performance gearing systems and understanding the tradeoffs between performance, robustness, manufacturability, and cost.

  • Enjoy operating at both subsystem and system levels, balancing actuator-level optimization with overall robot integration needs.

  • Are highly hands-on and enjoy building, debugging, instrumenting, and testing hardware directly.

  • Can move fluidly between first-principles analysis, rapid prototyping, and production-oriented engineering decisions.

  • Are comfortable working in fast-moving environments with evolving requirements and aggressive technical goals.

  • Have a strong sense of ownership and proactively drive cross-functional alignment to unblock progress.

  • Communicate clearly across disciplines and can collaborate effectively with research, controls, manufacturing, and operations teams.

jobs.title: Senior RTL Design Engineer – Interconnect & Network Datapath
jobs.description_html:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. Building on efforts like Jalapeño, the team is developing future generations of AI-native silicon and tightly integrated systems to power the next generation of frontier models. By co-designing chips, systems, tools, and methodologies, the team helps deliver faster, more efficient, and production-ready hardware for OpenAI’s supercomputing platform.

About the Role

We are looking for a highly experienced, hands-on RTL engineer with deep packet-networking and interconnect expertise to own critical on- and off-chip communication components for our custom AI accelerator platform.

You will drive the microarchitecture and RTL implementation of scalable on-chip fabrics connecting high-bandwidth compute, memory, and I/O subsystems, as well as purpose-built off-chip interfaces and protocols that enable custom computing at scale. The ideal candidate has recently owned production RTL for networking or packet-switched datapaths such as Ethernet switches, NICs, SmartNICs, network accelerators, RDMA/RoCE systems, NoCs, or custom scale-up/scale-out fabrics.

This is a senior engineering role with broad technical ownership and substantial direct RTL work. You will drive designs from requirements and performance analysis through microarchitecture, SystemVerilog implementation, verification closure, physical design convergence, silicon bring-up, and production readiness. You will also plan and oversee the work of junior engineers and help develop productive engineering relationships with external partners.

In this role, you will:

  • Own the microarchitecture, RTL design, and delivery of major packet-based interconnect and networking components, including NoC fabrics, switches, routers, bridges, protocol adapters, arbiters, queues, schedulers, buffers, and traffic-management logic.

  • Design mechanisms for routing, arbitration, ordering, flow control, congestion management, quality of service, packet scheduling, buffering, and performance monitoring.

  • Develop on-chip and off-chip interfaces, protocol bridges, and custom networking protocols or protocol extensions for scale-up and scale-out systems.

  • Perform substantial direct microarchitecture, SystemVerilog coding, simulation, and debug work.

  • Collaborate with architecture and performance teams to analyze traffic patterns, identify bottlenecks, and optimize latency, bandwidth, fairness, and utilization under realistic workloads.

  • Work with verification teams to develop coverage plans, assertions, stress scenarios, and debug strategies for highly concurrent packet and fabric behavior.

  • Partner with physical design teams on floorplan-aware design, pipeline strategy, timing closure, power, area, and physical congestion.

  • Collaborate with firmware, software, validation, and post-silicon teams through bring-up and production readiness.

  • Drive third-party engagements involving networking, interface protocols, and silicon IP while maintaining design quality and execution accountability.

  • Provide technical leadership through architecture and design reviews, documentation, mentoring, and reusable RTL methodologies.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

  • Extensive industry experience with recent, hands-on ownership of complex networking, packet-processing, or packet-switched interconnect RTL.

  • Demonstrated networking expertise in one or more of the following: Ethernet switching, NIC/SmartNIC/DPU datapaths, network accelerators, RDMA/RoCE, InfiniBand, traffic management, or custom scale-up/scale-out transports.

  • Deep expertise in Verilog/SystemVerilog and the development of clean, parameterized, production-quality RTL.

  • A strong record of owning major RTL blocks or SoC subsystems from requirements and microarchitecture through tape-out and silicon bring-up.

  • Experience designing queues, arbiters, schedulers, buffers, routing logic, virtual channels, credit-based flow control, congestion management, quality of service, ordering, or deadlock-avoidance mechanisms.

  • Experience with relevant on-chip, chip-to-chip, or host interfaces such as AXI, CHI, CXL, PCIe, or Ethernet, alongside deeper networking or packet-datapath expertise.

  • Experience designing custom networking protocols, protocol extensions, or hardware datapaths for large-scale RDMA/RoCE, HPC, or AI systems.

  • Strong familiarity with RTL development and signoff flows, including lint, CDC/RDC, synthesis, formal verification, static timing analysis, power analysis, and design-for-test considerations.

  • Experience collaborating with architecture, verification, physical design, firmware, performance, and post-silicon teams to deliver complex silicon.

  • Strong judgment when balancing performance, power, area, schedule, verification risk, and physical implementation constraints.

  • The ability to provide technical direction, mentor engineers, and drive alignment while remaining actively involved in RTL design and debugging.

  • A passion for reducing complexity and improving engineering leverage through automation and pragmatic design.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience designing packet-switched interconnect or networking datapaths for AI accelerators, GPUs, CPUs, HPC systems, NICs/SmartNICs, switch ASICs, or large-scale datacenter silicon.

  • Experience addressing virtualization, isolation, RAS, telemetry, security, or memory-consistency requirements within complex networking or interconnect subsystems.

  • Experience with network or NoC performance modeling, traffic simulation, emulation, FPGA prototyping, or post-silicon traffic and performance analysis.

  • Experience leading architecture or RTL delivery for first-generation networking or interconnect IP in rapidly evolving silicon programs.

jobs.description_html:
About the Team

OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. The Engineering Acceleration team builds products that multiply the effectiveness of OpenAI’s technical teams, helping engineers, researchers, and product teams understand complex systems, learn from what they ship, and operate reliably at scale.

As AI changes how software is built, we have an opportunity to rethink engineering workflows from first principles. We’re creating tools and shared systems that turn complex data, experimentation, and technical workflows into clear decisions and useful action.

About the Role

In this role, you’ll lead design across two connected product areas: a real-time data exploration and observability experience for investigating large-scale system and product behavior, and an experimentation platform for safely launching changes, measuring their impact, and deciding whether to ramp, iterate, or roll back.

This is more than a dashboard-design role. You’ll define the interaction models that take someone from a vague question or unexpected signal to a trustworthy answer and clear next step. You’ll work closely with engineers, researchers, data scientists, and product teams to understand the mechanics of their work and make dense technical systems coherent without flattening the details that matter.

You’ll also help establish greater consistency across OpenAI’s enterprise and internal tools, developing durable patterns that support AI-native workflows and enable other designers to build more effectively.

This role is based in our Seattle, WA or San Francisco, CA offices. We offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Lead end-to-end design for data-intensive products used by engineers, researchers, and product teams.

  • Make complex concepts—including data freshness, coverage, reliability, uncertainty, experiment assignment, metric validity, rollout state, and regressions—understandable and actionable.

  • Partner closely with engineering, data science, research, and product management to translate deeply technical infrastructure into elegant, coherent product experiences.

  • Use prototyping, research, and rigorous design exploration to establish interaction patterns for emerging technical and AI-native workflows.

  • Define shared systems and patterns that create consistency across OpenAI’s enterprise and internal tools.

  • Establish a high bar for information architecture, visual hierarchy, interaction quality, and craft across complex, multi-surface products.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Proven track record of leading operational and technical activities in large-scale data centers.

  • Extensive expertise in MEP design, operation, and maintenance, including critical infrastructure systems.

  • Comprehensive knowledge of data center buildings, equipment, and operational workflows.

  • Deep understanding of power, cooling, networking, and construction systems.

jobs.description_html:
About the Team

OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. The Identity team builds the foundational systems that enable people, organizations, devices, and agents to securely access OpenAI products.

The team works across consumer and enterprise experiences, including account structures, sign-in, authentication, recovery, privacy, permissions, administration, and agent identity. As AI systems become increasingly capable of acting on behalf of people and organizations, we are defining new models for authorization and trust across human-to-agent and agent-to-agent interactions.

About the Role

In this role, you’ll lead design for foundational identity experiences across OpenAI’s products. You’ll make permissions, access, risk, and administration feel clear, safe, and genuinely usable—whether someone is securing a personal account, administering access across an enterprise, signing in to another product with ChatGPT, or authorizing an agent to perform sensitive work.

Your work will span established identity challenges and emerging interaction models without established design conventions. You’ll help define how users understand what an agent can access, who or what it is acting on behalf of, and when confirmation or stronger authentication should appear. Working closely with product, engineering, security, privacy, and design, you’ll translate complex policies and technical systems into coherent, trustworthy experiences.

This role is based in our San Francisco HQ. We offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Lead the design direction for identity, account security, permissions, and administrative experiences across OpenAI’s consumer and enterprise products.

  • Design and ship high-quality experiences spanning sign-in, authentication, account recovery, device accounts, privacy, access controls, governance, and remediation.

  • Help users understand what people, systems, and agents can access or do on their behalf.

jobs.title: Product Designer
jobs.description_html:
Outset invented a better way to do research: AI-powered user interviews.

Global brands like Hubspot, Microsoft, Uber and Nestle use Outset to achieve deeper, qualitative insights about their users at unprecedented speed and scale.

The research industry is massive (>$140B and growing) and ripe for disruption. Incumbents are outdated, slow, and burdened by high-cost services. That's our opportunity.


Outset is backed by top Silicon Valley investors and raised a $30M Series B in December 2025—less than six months after our Series A—led by Radical Ventures with participation from M12 (Microsoft’s venture arm), 8VC, Y Combinator, and Adverb Ventures.

The raise follows a breakout year, with our business growing 8x as enterprise customers across industries adopt our category, AI‑moderated research, as the new standard for understanding people.

We’re a tight-knit team serving some of the world’s largest enterprises.

We're looking for a Product Designer with excellent craft and strong technical range, someone who can shape intuitive, elegant experiences that feel like magic while also being fluent in the AI-assisted coding and prototyping workflows that are becoming core to modern design practice.

You're excited to own problems end-to-end in a fast, AI-native product team, working closely with our Founding Designer and the rest of product and engineering to design generative product experiences that are as functional as they are beautiful - often owning the full arc from the kernel of an idea to a working, coded prototype.

Responsibilities

  • Partner with Design, Product and Engineering to craft experiences that drive business impact.

  • Create wireframes, prototypes, and high-fidelity visuals for new and existing features — and build functional, front-to-back prototypes in code when that's the fastest path to a real answer.

  • Use AI coding tools (Claude Code, Cursor, or similar) as a core part of your design process — not an occasional accelerant, but the way you move from idea to working software.

  • Push full-stack code (HTML/CSS/JS, Python or similar) confidently enough to prototype, iterate, and occasionally ship to production.

  • Operate comfortably in a real dev environment: git workflows, local setup, reading PRs, and collaborating closely with engineers.

  • Conduct user research and usability testing to ensure designs are user-centered and data-informed.

  • Contribute to a consistent, accessible design system.

  • Work from our San Francisco office at least 4 days per week, collaborating in person with design, product, and engineering.

Qualifications

  • Experience designing digital products (or equivalent depth of experience), ideally in startup or SaaS environments where you've owned significant product surfaces.

  • Exceptional design taste and strong point of view on craft — a portfolio that demonstrates real UX and visual design judgment, not just polish.

  • Proficiency with design tools (Figma, Claude Design, etc.)

  • Excellent communication and storytelling skills — able to present design decisions clearly and succinctly.

  • A growth mindset and willingness to experiment, iterate, and learn quickly.

  • Demonstrated ability to write and ship full-stack code - some combination of HTML/CSS/JS and Python - even if design is your primary craft.

  • Real, hands-on fluency with AI coding assistants (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.) as day-to-day tools, not novelty - you reach for them naturally to explore ideas, prototype interactions, and move faster than a traditional design-then-handoff process allows.

  • Comfort operating in a dev environment (git, terminal, local builds) and reviewing/discussing code with engineers.

  • Experience collaborating in agile, cross-functional teams.

jobs.title: Brand Designer, Growth
jobs.description_html:
We're looking for a Growth Brand Designer to sit at the intersection of brand craft and growth performance. You'll be the designer who makes Perplexity's highest-volume, highest-leverage marketing surfaces — paid ads, social, lifecycle email, and campaign assets — look unmistakably Perplexity while actually moving the numbers.

This is a shipping role, but it's equally a thinking role. Strategic concepting is a big part of the job: you'll sit with the Growth team as an ideator — generating campaign concepts, testing hypotheses, and shaping the creative strategy behind the work — not just executing briefs handed to you. The ideas you bring to the table matter as much as the assets you ship.

You'll produce a steady stream of ad and campaign creative across formats and channels, then work with Growth to read the results and iterate. You care about conversion and craft in equal measure: you'd never ship an off-brand asset to win a test, and you'd never hide behind polish when the data says a concept isn't working.

You'll report into the Brand/Creative Studio team and work closely with Growth, Product Marketing, Brand, and our motion and web designers.

What you'll do

  • Drive strategic concepting for growth campaigns — bring original ideas, angles, and creative territories to the table, and shape the brief rather than just receiving it

  • Operate as a true ideation partner to the Growth team: co-develop campaign strategy, propose test hypotheses, and pitch concepts that open up new creative directions

  • Own the design of growth creative end-to-end — paid social and display ads, campaign assets, and lifecycle email — from concept to shipped asset

  • Design for volume and velocity: build variant sets, test hypotheses, and iterate on winners with the Growth team using real performance data

  • Turn product launches and GTM campaigns into ad creative that lands on every channel it runs — static, animated, and everything in between

  • Build and maintain scalable ad and email templates so high-frequency asset production stays fast and on-brand

  • Partner with Brand to keep visual consistency across every growth touchpoint as our brand system evolves

  • Collaborate with our motion designer and web designer so campaigns feel cohesive from the first ad impression to the landing page

  • Bring a strong point of view on what makes performance creative great — and push back when a "best practice" would cheapen the brand

What we're looking for

  • A strong portfolio of growth and brand design work — paid ads, social campaigns, lifecycle email, campaign systems — that shows both craft and results

  • Proven strategic concepting ability: you can show campaigns where the idea was yours, not just the execution, and articulate the thinking behind them

  • Excellent visual design skills with a clear sense of brand, typography, layout, and composition

  • Hands-on experience designing performance creative at a consumer or prosumer tech company, including working directly with growth or performance marketing teams

  • Fluency reading creative performance data (CTR, conversion, hook rates) and translating it into design decisions

  • Ability to work fast, manage a high volume of deliverables across channels, and iterate quickly without dropping the quality bar

  • Fluency in Figma and the Adobe Creative Suite

  • An instinct for building repeatable systems — templates, variant frameworks, asset kits — rather than one-off files

  • 5+ years of industry experience

Nice to have

  • Motion design skills — animated ads, short-form video for social, or After Effects fluency

  • Familiarity with ad platform specs and constraints (Meta, Google, TikTok, X, YouTube) and how they shape creative decisions

  • Experience using AI-assisted design and image-generation workflows to scale creative output

  • Copywriting instincts — you can tighten a headline when there's no writer in the room

jobs.title: Design Systems Lead
jobs.location: San Francisco / Remote (United States) / New York City
jobs.description_html:
About the role

We're seeking a Design Systems Lead with extensive experience owning design systems at large organizations. You'll bootstrap an intuitive semantic token system that supports design and product teams across multiple platforms and frameworks - the foundation that keeps Perplexity's product coherent as we scale.

This is a true 50/50 design-engineer role. You'll live primarily in GitHub, where you own the system's repo, while staying fluent in Figma so design and engineering never drift apart. You'll set the bar for visual quality and the technical standards that let feature teams move fast without fragmenting the experience.

You'll work at the intersection of design and engineering, partnering with product feature teams across mobile, web, and React surfaces.

What you'll do

  • Bootstrap and own an intuitive semantic token system that works across multiple platforms and frameworks

  • Own the design system repo on GitHub: the source of truth for components, tokens, and standards, including versioning, release management, and a clear changelog

  • Set and uphold a high bar for visual design quality across every surface the system touches

  • Navigate the nuanced differences between mobile, web, and React UI best practices, and encode them into the system

  • Define and run the contribution model and governance: review and shepherd inbound contributions from product feature teams, keeping quality and consistency high as the system grows

  • Keep design and engineering in sync, bridging Figma and code so the system stays coherent end-to-end

  • Own clear, first-class documentation so teams can adopt components and tokens on their own, and drive adoption across the org through onboarding, office hours, and hands-on support

  • Bake in accessibility (WCAG) and theming (including dark mode) as defaults, not afterthoughts

  • Maintain a system roadmap, balancing net-new work, migrations, and deprecations against feature-team needs

  • Bring new AI tooling into the design systems workflow and help shape how we build systems in an AI-native way

  • Operate with autonomy in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment

What we're looking for

  • Extensive experience owning design systems at large organizations

  • A true 50/50 design-engineer, equally credible in visual craft and in code

  • An impeccable eye for visual design

  • Deep understanding of the nuanced differences between mobile, web, and React UI best practices

  • Strong product sensibilities to help evaluate and integrate contributions from various product feature teams

  • Fluency in Figma, but primarily living in GitHub where you own the repo

  • Experience designing and maintaining semantic design tokens and scalable component APIs

  • A track record of driving adoption through excellent documentation and cross-functional partnership

  • Working knowledge of accessibility standards (WCAG) and how to build them into a system

  • Readiness to work with new AI tooling and genuine comfort with ambiguity

Nice to have

  • Experience building a semantic token system from scratch across multiple platforms

  • A track record scaling a design system through a period of fast org growth

  • Experience defining contribution models and governance for multi-team design systems

  • Familiarity with component tooling and documentation platforms (e.g., Storybook)

  • Experience mentoring designers and engineers and growing a design systems practice

jobs.title: Lead Product Designer, Growth
jobs.description_html:
Perplexity is looking for an experienced Lead Product Designer to own design for Growth. You'll shape the experiences that bring Perplexity to as many people as possible — making software that feels like the future but can be understood and used by anyone in the world today.

Growth design has its own craft and nuance. You'll own the highest-leverage moments in the user journey: first-run onboarding and activation, consumer acquisition surfaces, conversion and upsell flows, paywalls and pricing, and the retention loops that turn first-time users into daily ones. This is design where a few pixels or a single step can move real numbers, so you'll pair a high craft bar with rigorous experimentation — shipping constantly and letting real data guide the work.

You care about clarity, craft, details, and delight as much as you care about growth and impact. This role is deeply cross-functional: you'll partner closely with our Growth and Product Marketing teams to align on positioning, messaging, and funnel strategy, and you care about everything it takes to make a product great: product, interaction, brand, growth, copywriting, engineering, and marketing.

What you'll do

  • Lead product design for Growth across the full funnel — acquisition, onboarding, activation, conversion, upsells, and retention

  • Design first-run and onboarding experiences that get users to value as fast as possible

  • Craft consumer acquisition and activation surfaces, and conversion/upsell flows including paywalls, pricing, and plan comparison

  • Partner closely with Growth and Product Marketing on positioning, messaging, landing experiences, and funnel strategy

  • Design and run experiments, using data and real usage to drive decisions and measure impact

  • Ship features that balance well-established UI paradigms with novel applications of AI

  • Think about how to go from 0→1 but also how to make your decisions scale well

  • Contribute to process so we're always shipping changes you're proud of, as often as possible

  • Partner with brand design to ensure our growth surfaces are not only effective but memorable

What we're looking for

  • Experience designing consumer or prosumer products, with a strong track record in growth design

  • Deep understanding of growth nuances: onboarding, activation, acquisition, conversion, upsells, paywalls, pricing, and retention

  • A data-informed approach — fluent in experimentation, funnels, and metrics, and comfortable learning from usage

  • Experience partnering with Growth, Product Marketing, and cross-functional teams on messaging and funnel strategy

  • Comfortable thinking about both 0→1 product design and large-scale optimization

  • Excellent visual, UI, and interaction skills

  • An excellent communicator with team members and users

  • You care about shipping great software more than anything else

  • 5+ years of industry experience

Nice to have

  • Comfort prototyping or coding your ideas

  • Some of our design team writes production code — we welcome existing skills or interest in coding with React or SwiftUI

jobs.title: Lead Product Designer, Enterprise
jobs.description_html:
Perplexity is looking for a Lead Product Designer to own the design of our enterprise product. You'll design new experiences across enterprise and multiplayer use cases — making software that feels like the future but can be understood and used by anyone in the world today.

These surfaces are net-new and, in many cases, unprecedented. You'll be building them 0→1, which means bringing deep knowledge of how enterprise software actually works: organizational and seat management, and deeply nuanced role-based experiences that account for workplace policy, compliance, administrative management, privacy, permissions, and security. You'll ship features that balance well-established UI paradigms with novel applications of AI, working independently and strategically to find both the problems worth solving and the solutions worth shipping.

Good design that nobody gets to use is wasted, so you'll optimize for getting great software into customers' hands and learning from real usage. You'll work closely with product, engineering, and the broader design team, and you care about everything it takes to make a product great: product, interaction, brand, growth, copywriting, engineering, and marketing.

What you'll do

  • Design net-new, 0→1 enterprise surfaces across enterprise and general multiplayer use cases

  • Design for the realities of enterprise software: organizational management, seat management, admin controls, permissions, privacy, security, and compliance

  • Craft deeply nuanced role-based experiences that adapt to workplace policy and different levels of access and responsibility

  • Partner with brand design to ensure the enterprise product is not only useful but memorable
